## ACTIVE PRODUCTION — MIDSUMMER ACT I / NEW META WINDOW / CLIPS 001–218

**NUMBERED CAST PULL / FOUR GROUPS:** Use the [live numbered cast guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11q213HYI0gSOnkXuqNkMq_6hYwMdFA8i50q-_PXdQDs/edit). Every one of the 218 entries embeds CAST PULL inside its META FRAME: scene identities, visible support, represented likenesses, numbered singer or NO VOCALS, entrances/exits and required sheet groups. A = Athenian/court references 01–08 plus court/background slots 26–30; B = Mechanical/workshop references 17–22 plus existing helper slots 23–25; C = ether court 09–12; D = ether service nodes 13–16. Principals stay 01–22; the eight existing silent/background functions use 23–30, with no new sung words. The current Act I entries call for at most A+B, or one group; truly empty views say NONE. The other chat is formatting the four grouped images. The guide distinguishes that in-progress layout from the six actual legacy JPEGs: do not claim an undelivered composite or support portrait already exists, and do not search for 23–30 inside the old 22-character sheets. Use the numbered grouped blocks actually supplied in the renderer window and its established appearances. Include silent visible people and recognizable stored likenesses in the pull; a theatrical role stays on its actor's original number.

**ACTIVE BREATHING EDITION — RESTART AT CLIP 001:** The current complete Act I is 218 films in 22 batches: 193 unchanged dialogue units plus 25 intentionally nonvocal films (172 seconds of planned entrances, exits, reactions and empty-set views). BATCH 22 ends with CLIPS 211–218: https://docs.google.com/document/d/124Zso2bUBn_AQcXaeC3mCLuLSIJHZACawYjfd6s9VNY/edit?usp=drivesdk. Start at CLIP 001, the castle establishing shot; CLIP 002 is the empty court, CLIP 003 the initial entrance, and CLIP 004 the first original Theseus words. CLIP counts actual films. SOURCE DIALOGUE 001–193 identifies the preserved source text and never resets the output count.

**PER-CLIP META FRAME / MUSIC:** Send each complete entry's META FRAME, REFERENCE, TIMING, PERFORMANCE / AUDIO and BACKGROUND / CAMERA. Each states its own setting, named characters, cyborg / pure robot / marble mana bodies, pocket-dimension context and actual action. Sung verse is the default. Use expressive sung recitative or poetic rap for prose, a difficult melodic passage or a voice unable to sustain the tune, preserving every assigned word, singer, stress and musical intention. Listeners remain silent except the six-worker ALL ensemble.

**PLANNED SILENCE IS PERFORMANCE:** A NO VOCALS entry has no singing, rap, recitative, humming, voiceover or added sonnet. Empty-set shots contain no people of any kind, including robots and marble people. Show entrances/exits crossing actual thresholds and give the room time before or after. For this film use complete 6–10-second setting views, 6–8-second entrance/exit films, and 1–2-second reaction holds where words fit or the separately scored 6-second silent reactions. These durations are production choices, not a fixed industry rule or measured rendered audio. Never compress the original text or fill these designated rests. The prior 193-film counter described the earlier unpaused edition; the active render order is 001–218.

**ACTIVE DRAMATIC CONFLICT:** Athenians = cyborgs; Mechanicals = pure robots; the ether court = marble mana people fabricated by machines. Cyborg makers constructed the machines, and those machines construct the mana people; cyborg bodies also depend on manufactured parts. The dispute is who may claim to be a person, a construct or an owner. The selected master and every one of its 193 dialogue camera entries, with 25 additional nonvocal films carry this through the existing Shakespeare action; perform the same complete SING words and speakers. See [current faction and material canon](https://github.com/IsekaiSensei/chat.work.open.ai/blob/main/COOKBOOK.md#midsummer--three-societies-and-the-makers-claim).

This new-window rerun selects [MIDSUMMER ACT I MASTER](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jauzJXquc-sX7v-vAqOf4oIafjk-KXSUuLWC6jdkiWc/edit) → [BATCH 01 / CLIPS 001–010](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Jm3B8Jx4RZte_kBjOxoBLWjuHrnR4ipJTC6gpz2o-6U/edit) → each batch's printed NEXT BATCH link, through BATCH 22 / CLIPS 211–218. This is not The Uninvited King, the 000–009 workbench plan, an archive or a generic retelling by Shakespeare. Read the full batch before rendering; use its exact assigned words or explicit NO VOCALS designation and its own META FRAME, PERFORMANCE / AUDIO and BACKGROUND/CAMERA fields. Each ten-second film stands independently. Keep performer, face, costume, visible noun, physical action and result sourced from the specific batch.

**CAST SOURCE — SIX APPROVED CLEAN CHARACTER JPEG SHEETS:** [01–04 Athenians A](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A6kT9xVJXDy_JpktinAre0b4OazYzLc9/view) · [05–08 Athenians B](https://drive.google.com/file/d/12HkMoHLRiW84W72-XEoiKw7In81VWsx0/view) · [09–12 Fairies A](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1kPJNjrmq_nNKnNCRghDV0fJQ_i78DhUb/view) · [13–16 Fairies B](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1MaVEO6_4CUi5OThHtv8ojkTY_Muv5D8C/view) · [17–20 Mechanicals A](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ztxe_nt21aWQn33hdCHITup_PUibakyg/view) · [21–22 Mechanicals B](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1bkMqGeV3UiIL1jW2PEw0Zq4wjJzukpDB/view). Select the numbered visual block for each on-screen character. Shakespeare is the AUTHOR OF THE WORDS, not a generic on-screen actor. THESEUS, HIPPOLYTA, EGEUS, HERMIA, LYSANDER, DEMETRIUS, HELENA, PHILOSTRATE, BOTTOM, QUINCE, FLUTE, SNOUT, SNUG and STARVELING are distinct cast roles; no invented generic Shakespeare face or costume. For Act I the singer is the actor printed before each SING line.

**ESTABLISHED CAST — CONTINUE WITHOUT RE-UPLOAD LOOPS:** Preserve the six approved clean MIDSUMMER_CAST sheets and the exact numbered actor appearances ALREADY used successfully in this Meta production window. Reuse the established actors' numbered identities, face shapes, hair, costumes and equipment; apply the owner's current cyborg / pure robot / marble mana body materials as specified in the active master and batches; a Drive link is an archival identifier, not a request to download or regenerate a character each clip. Do not infer that an image is unavailable merely because its Drive sharing is private: the owner reports Meta previously used these references successfully. Never substitute a generic Shakespeare portrait, generic robot presenter, replacement cast, or newly invented face. No repetitive 'upload again' request, re-verification gate, reboot, fresh scene selection or restart. If a genuine renderer error prevents use of a specific previously available asset, state the actual error once without falsely declaring all references inaccessible. Character performance remains the foreground; the workshop and product demonstrations are supporting physical actions.

**PRODUCTION FILE ROLES:** MASTER/BATCH = words, singer and camera directions for this particular Midsummer run. [Google Dailies](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RrNJYm7kHj_6lq-CJVuloR2sCuXgFsLQqBfGp1njh1Y/edit) = actual outputs and Ryan's verdict. [GitHub META](META.md) = QC policy only. [GitHub COOKBOOK](COOKBOOK.md) = source visual law. [GitHub ORDERS](ORDERS.md) / [Google ORDERS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qHzHhlbDweQQrqcOT8rxuurhSO9SpKmRWs4iqY-CWzc/edit) = live routing. The origin manuscript is a different source, not fallback dialogue for this rerun.

**NEW META WINDOW — COMPLETE SHAKESPEARE RERUN (2026-11-06 OWNER DECISION):** Ryan reports the entire preceding Meta Shakespeare/Midsummer render attempt failed his direction and continuity QC because of pervasive drift. That attempt is REJECTED as the active take set; do not resume its window, carry over its last take counter, or mark any of its outputs accepted. Ryan is personally rerunning the COMPLETE selected Act I set in a wholly NEW Meta window. Start that new window at **CLIP 001 / BATCH 01**, then advance consecutively through **CLIP 218 / BATCH 22** (last batch contains 211–218), with the same complete verbatim Shakespeare assigned SING lines and the noun-in-shot, physical DNA inventory repair, proper pocket dimension, performer and camera directions below. Each clip remains an independently complete short. Do not abbreviate, silently skip, claim a previously rendered clip suffices, insert a fresh approval loop, or substitute the Uninvited King source. These are Ryan's QC and rerun instructions; they do not mean the renderer has completed any new take. Preserve the prior files/receipts as historical rejected attempts for provenance, not current progress.

**LIVE META PERFORMANCE — SHAKESPEARE / VISIBLE NOUN / PHYSICAL REPAIR (2026-11-06):** In the ongoing Shakespeare/Midsummer render, the **only sung/spoken words are the complete, consecutive, already assigned William Shakespeare lines**, performed by the assigned character; maintain the same music, singer, order and musical pace. Do not substitute a separate origin-story screenplay, modern narration, invented lyrics, summary, repeated verse or production-instruction narration. Each batch contains ten consecutive clips (the final Act I batch has eight); keep rendering the assigned sequence until its assigned scope is complete. The clip is a complete short film with a visible cause, purposeful operation and recognizable result, without edit/stitching notes.

**NOUN-IN-SHOT — CINEMATOGRAPHER RULE:** When a performer says a concrete noun (person, object, place, component, tool, inventory item), the audience SEES that actual noun in the shot at that utterance, preferably physically in the performer's or worker's hand when it can be handled. Follow the *same* identifiable noun/prop and its cause → physical action → result; show literal nouns first, then stage metaphors visually without replacing the literal action. A dialogue line about a sword must show a sword, not an arbitrary glowing symbol. Camera direction points to the noun as it is sung. Never put these instructions in singer dialogue, voiceover, captions, or an invented storyboard outside the active camera field.

**IN → FIX → OUT — REQUIRED VISIBLE DEMONSTRATION:** At an appropriate sword/injury/repair beat in the current Shakespeare camera plan, show one **ordinary inventory item** with one identifiable break, its generic inventory square, and the item physically leaving the user's position through the SMALL local double-helix transfer seam. The camera sees that **same damaged item** arrive on the **quantum table inside the pocket dimension opened by the MAIN DNA wormhole**. Show a technician/assistant performing an intelligible mechanical repair on the original part, demonstrating the break is corrected; send that **same now repaired item back upward through the same local helix**, into the same user's hand/slot; the original inventory square visibly updates from damaged to restored on actual receipt. One item, one journey, one repair, one return. No teleport duplication, no unexplained transformation, no random replacement prop, no generic sparkle standing in for the fix. Keep the world's entrance helix (access to the entire dimension) distinct from the smaller object-transfer opening. Film it as an actual short action within the existing shot, not as an editorial bridge or mandatory repeat in every clip.

**FILES AND ROLES:** The already selected native [Midsummer Act I master](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jauzJXquc-sX7v-vAqOf4oIafjk-KXSUuLWC6jdkiWc/edit) and its linked twenty-two batch Docs supply the exact Shakespeare words and assigned speakers for that run; the cinematic directions live in each batch's BACKGROUND/camera field. The separately selected [Uninvited King MAIN](https://docs.google.com/document/d/12QzK2VKN0EM-QjSxmH08BtLMeIBcxpu8a0Q4Odzu2po/edit?tab=t.o59y58g80007) remains a different approved manuscript, NOT a substitute for a Folger/Midsummer window. Only Ryan's direct selection changes which source is active. Do not modify the printed Shakespeare lines to fix a camera problem.

**DNA WORMHOLE → POCKET DIMENSION — GLOBAL META FRAME / ART DIRECTION (2026-11-06):** The visible, paired double-helix DNA wormhole is **the opening into the pocket dimension where the scene's quantum-workshop / ether action actually takes place**. The aperture opens that dimension and reveals its immense, inhabited, zero-G working space, with the established quantum table and physical crew **inside**. It is not decoration placed inside an otherwise unrelated room, and the pocket dimension must not appear to have an unrelated entrance. The smaller DNA-helix seam beside a material or inventory item is the same network's **local transfer opening**, not a substitute for the dimension-opening entrance. A scene already inside the pocket does not need a gratuitous repeated portal-opening shot: its environment remains the space opened by the DNA wormhole. Preserve other explicitly sourced passages (for example, the forest tree) and the selected scene's timing and images. This is visual/world direction, **not new lyrics, a title card, or a stitching instruction**.

## Source access and the owner's assignment

Ryan's latest direct assignment controls the selected script, passage, clip range and reference set. Preserve an explicit all-nine-images/every-clip instruction. Historical completion records describe their own runs; they do not cancel a later explicit owner assignment.

If a window can read only native Google Docs, use the [current readable Dailies](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RrNJYm7kHj_6lq-CJVuloR2sCuXgFsLQqBfGp1njh1Y/edit) and the linked native Google screenplay. The Dailies view preserves the existing ledger's wording. Dailies record progress; they do not choose replacement dialogue. An inaccessible TXT/MD/XLSX file is an access problem to solve, not a reason to pick another screenplay or reduce an assigned range. Use the owner-selected text already present in that window when available. Report the specific inaccessible source once while continuing accessible assigned work.

For creative development, Ryan translates lived reality directly into Chronicles of Sol: “the fourth wall and the third wall and the second wall are all the same wall.” Apply that method without adding explanatory captions, screenplay annotations or new scenes from examples he expressly excludes. Refer to [the World Book](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wiIjBtDvhunHwL7XHHaK-IFejjtd4SeIq-0z6vG7ofE/edit) for story canon and [Cookbook IB-01](https://github.com/IsekaiSensei/chat.work.open.ai/blob/main/COOKBOOK.md#ib-01--chronicles-of-sol--imperial-beach-station-and-relay-market) for the local references.

The current Midsummer edition's 25 explicit NO VOCALS films and its timed reaction/entrance/exit holds are fully assigned music-and-picture passages. Keep them free of words. The gap-filling instructions below apply only to genuinely unassigned material, never to those deliberate rests.

When there is a blank scene slot or an unassigned space in the performance, fill it with a musical comma or a sonnet passage that fits ten seconds. Pull the existing words from the **SONNETS — 10-second gap bank** tab in the [Google screenplay](https://docs.google.com/document/d/12QzK2VKN0EM-QjSxmH08BtLMeIBcxpu8a0Q4Odzu2po/edit); [matching source bank](https://github.com/IsekaiSensei/chat.work.open.ai/blob/main/production-sheets/SONNET_GAP_BANK_10S.json).

Choose passages randomly for the available spaces, keep the actual words and assigned singer, and write each chosen passage into its scene before performing it. Keep that selection for the run rather than choosing anew on each retry. A comma is a brief musical/physical breathing beat. An existing assigned line remains assigned; the filler occupies the space around it. Continue the authorized work without another permission loop because a blank was encountered.

For a selected source conversation, sing its actual words with the original speaker; a pasted quotation retains that speaker. For the active Midsummer assignment, retain every printed Act I SING line verbatim and the assigned character performer and voice. For the newly requested origin adaptation, sing the exact MAIN text with its printed singer assignments; the source register identifies new narration separately from historic owner dictation and recovered verse. Keep each assigned musical performance continuous.

Use Ryan's current selected reference set, with each sheet informing its own subject. [COOKBOOK.md](https://github.com/IsekaiSensei/chat.work.open.ai/blob/main/COOKBOOK.md) supplies visual details when needed.

A video assignment produces moving video. Deliver each successful output to Ryan, who handles QC, drift, flow, selection, editing and assembly. Render prompts contain the in-scene performance and camera action; omit stitching or editorial instructions.

Optional writing formats, repetition audits, QC notes and incomplete ledger fields do not add approval steps or suspend an existing assignment. Use the selected script rather than searching optional drafts for a replacement. Keep creative review separate from delivery; do not reject or rerender successful output on Ryan's behalf.

If a source link fails, use its matching accessible copy or the same source already loaded in the active window. Report an actual access or renderer error with the affected item once, and continue work that remains possible. Do not turn an aesthetic concern into a platform error, claim an unperformed render, substitute a still for a video, or bypass a real platform restriction.

- **Dailies:** actual output, source excerpt, singer, reference, take/file, duration, renderer result and Ryan's stated verdict.

Keep the existing file IDs. Add new source exchanges and actual takes in order. Retrieve archive material for a requested recovery or a specific source lookup; it is not part of the routine production pickup.
